question: Should ClickClack core own browser preview of DOCX and uploaded HTML in addition to inert text/code and the existing Markdown/PDF formats?
rationale: The implementation is careful and convincingly proven, but adopting third-party document parsing and hostile HTML rendering is a permanent product, dependency, and security-maintenance commitment that cannot be inferred from patch correctness.

options.title: Accept the full viewer
options.body: Own the bounded DOCX and uploaded-HTML preview paths in ClickClack core alongside the lower-risk formats.

options.title: Ship a narrower viewer
options.body: Merge code, text, Markdown, and PDF preview while deferring DOCX and uploaded HTML.

options.title: Keep downloads only
options.body: Decline the feature if maintainers do not want an in-browser artifact parser boundary in core.

recommendation.title: Accept the full viewer
recommendation.body: Own the bounded DOCX and uploaded-HTML preview paths in ClickClack core alongside the lower-risk formats.

likelyOwner.reason: The relevant upload, media, sanitizer, and chat-shell surfaces trace to the v0.1.0 release commit, making steipete the strongest available product-boundary owner.
